optional.without_it: inventory facts are unknown; offload and verify do not need it
LTC is not looked for in the audio of video files (WAV files are still checked with the standard library)
--proxy is refused (PROXY_UNAVAILABLE, nothing written); everything else works without it
--hash xxh64 is refused (HASH_UNAVAILABLE, nothing written); sha256 + c4 need only the standard library
fetch is refused (FETCH_UNAVAILABLE, nothing written); offload, verify and inventory do not need it

execution.overwrites: never: identical files are skipped, different ones are conflicts

never_recorded: credentials in URLs (userinfo, token / signature / key / password-like parameters)

follow.copies: appended bytes only, each appended range read back
follow.not_detected: whether the recorder still holds the file open (no portable API)
follow.seal_when: size and mtime unchanged for the settle window

not_provided: encoding proxies itself (offload --proxy queues ffmpeg-skill proxy; the encoder is ffmpeg-skill's)
deleting or formatting the source card
ASC MHL directory / root hashes, rename, flatten and collections (not yet)
recording a verify run as an ASC MHL generation (verify writes nothing)
authenticated downloads (cookies, logins, .netrc, browser cookies) and DRM-protected media (never circumvented)
playlists and channels (fetch takes the URL of one video)
Panasonic P2, Canon XF and RED card structures (their media are listed file by file, as generic)
interpreting AVCHD clip-info (.CPI) or Blackmagic RAW .sidecar contents (listed with their clip, not read)
grouping a recording continued on another card (each card is inventoried on its own)
telling whether a recorder still holds a growing file open (offload --follow seals on the settle window only)
decoding LTC (it is detected on a channel, its value comes from the container or the sidecar)
measuring sync offsets (sync groups are clock-based candidates for ffmpeg-skill multicam / sync)

progress.destination_speed: bytes written / time spent writing and syncing them (the drive's own speed, not the shared pace)
progress.slow_destination: a destination writing at under 50% of the destinations' median write speed, judged once each has written 64 MB; also in destinations[].warnings

proxy.hardware: ffmpeg-skill --hw when its doctor reports hw.platform_ok (VideoToolbox); otherwise its CPU encoder
proxy.made_from: the first verified copy, never the card

sync.ltc: detected (biphase-mark signal), never decoded; WAV with the standard library, other files with ffmpeg when on PATH

tools.description: Copy every file of a card or recorder folder to one or more destinations (the source is read once per file, written to every destination in parallel), verified by a sha256 (default) or xxh64 read-back of each; writes ingest-manifest.json and an ASC MHL history generation (ascmhl/) in each. With --follow, recordings still being written are copied as they grow (appended bytes only, each range read back), listed as growing partial copies, and sealed once unchanged for the settle window
Re-hash an offloaded folder against its manifest (sha256 or xxh64) and its ASC MHL history: missing, changed and unlisted files; writes nothing

Clip list of a card or an offloaded folder, one entry per recording: card structure (Sony XDCAM / XAVC, XDCAM EX, AVCHD, Blackmagic RAW, generic), spanned files grouped in order, camera sidecar metadata, reel / card id, manifest hash, ffprobe facts and sync facts (start timecode, frame rate, LTC on an audio channel, camera / recorder ids, wall-clock start). Given several folders, also the sync-group candidates: clips of different cards whose times overlap, for ffmpeg-skill multicam / sync

Download one video URL with yt-dlp (optional extra) into a staging folder, then offload it to every destination exactly like a card (verified copies, ingest-manifest.json, ASC MHL history); the manifest records the source URL (credentials redacted), the extractor, the yt-dlp version, the format id and the time
